name: Starter motor
summary: A strong electric motor that spins the engine to get it started.
whatItDoes: An engine can't start itself from rest. The starter turns the crankshaft fast enough for the engine to fire and run on its own.
howItWorks: When you turn the key or press start, a solenoid on the starter pushes a small gear (the pinion) into the teeth around the engine's flywheel, and closes a heavy-duty switch. The motor then draws a large current from the battery and spins the engine. As soon as the engine runs, the pinion pulls back out.
failureSymptoms: A single click and no crank
The starter keeps whirring after the engine starts
Starting problems that come and go
safetyNotes: Disconnect the battery first. The starter's main cable is always live.
It is heavier than it looks. Support it as the last bolt comes out.
